`e2e/artifacts/manifest/<state id>` from capture-manifest.spec.ts. Neither name is
a screen id from `.dfl-ux-paths/flows.json`, and two of them (`not-found` vs
So the mapping is DATA, stated once, and `publish-capture.mjs` refuses to guess it.
A screen renamed on either side goes RED here with both names printed, instead of
quietly publishing an index row with a null screenshot and calling it coverage.
why_only_two: The hermetic run photographs what a signed-out visitor can see. Of the 31 declared
screens, 7 render without a session and 24 redirect to /login — and of those 7 only
proves the other five with a marker and a settle measurement rather than with a
2 of 31 is therefore the honest number for this substrate, and it is published as
such: the other 29 screens are indexed with a NULL digest, which is the coverage
signal the schema is built to carry.
The authenticated capture (`capture-live.ts`, 26 of 31) is a different run with a
different credential and is NOT what this workflow does.
why_the_role_is_not_plain_anonymous: `ux_map_captures` has no substrate column, and the lens's primary read is `the
newest capture of this app in this role`. A signed-out capture of the LIVE
substrate already exists under role `anonymous` with 7 of 31 screens. Publishing
this thinner hermetic capture under the same role would make the weekly cron
overwrite the richer capture as `current`, every Monday.
`role` is free text by the RPC's own contract (roles are per-application), so the
substrate travels in the role name and again in the coverage note.
why_the_viewport_is_a_column_and_not_par: ADR-8 of plan `20260902-ux-paths-responsive-mobile-capture`, after Tainan answered
Q3 = B: the viewport is a COLUMN on `engineering.ux_map_captures`
(`viewport text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'desktop'`, unique key `(app_uuid, role, viewport,
digest)`). It is NOT a `<role>@mobile` suffix — that earlier design doubled the human
validation work and leaked a pseudo-role into every reader of `role`.
So the role below stays `anonymous-hermetic` for BOTH passes, and the two captures of
one build are distinguished by the `viewport` argument alone. `publish-capture.mjs
--viewport mobile` writes the mobile row; the default writes the desktop one.
why_screens_is_the_desktop_map: `screens` is the map for the DEFAULT viewport (`desktop`), and it keeps that name
because every publish before the mobile pass read it. A non-default viewport gets its
own map under `screens_by_viewport`, so the desktop publish is byte-unchanged.
why_the_mobile_map_is_the_same_two_scree: EXACTLY the two the desktop map publishes, so both viewports report 2 of 31 and the
viewer's switcher always has both siblings or neither. A wider mobile set would give
five screens a mobile image with NO desktop sibling — and the switcher (T3) was built
for the opposite case, `mobile absent`, so it would render a dead desktop button.
The directories differ from the desktop ones and that is not an oversight: the desktop
photographs of `login` and `not_found` are taken by `capture-regions.spec.ts` (under
`regions/`), while the mobile ones are taken by the `manifest-mobile` project (under
`manifest/`, suffixed `@390x844` per ADR-3). The map is DATA precisely so that this
kind of asymmetry is stated once instead of being guessed by a script.
Widening the mobile set means adding a screen id HERE and to `viewports[].capture_routes`
in `e2e/support/capture-manifest.json` — two data edits, no code.
